pages.title: Luca AI product documentation
intro: Luca is an AI analyst for e-commerce brands. It reads the data you connect from your store, ad platforms, analytics, payment and accounting tools, and answers your questions about the business in plain English.

Luca works done-with-you. Luca's team onboards each client directly, and a human stays in the loop: Luca does not change your connected systems on its own. This documentation is for buyers evaluating Luca, and for anyone who needs an exact account of what the product does today.

sections.title: How this documentation is organised
paragraphs: Products describes what Luca does, including Numbers, the reconciled view of your business. Integrations describes the data sources Luca connects to and, where it applies, which ones are set up by Luca's team.

Solutions describes the same capabilities from the point of view of a specific buyer, such as a founder, a finance lead or a subscription brand. Pricing explains how plans are published, including currencies and partner pricing.

Security explains how your data is handled, including the commitments in Luca's privacy policy. Onboarding and support explains how Luca's team sets you up and works with you. Coverage lists what this version documents and what is still waiting for confirmation.

sections.title: What is documented here
paragraphs: This version documents only capabilities that MaximusLabs has confirmed from Luca's product, website and team. Where a capability has a limit, for example it is set up by Luca's team or confirmed per account, the page states that limit.

Anything not yet confirmed is left out of this version. It is listed for Luca's team to confirm, and it will be documented once it is. If you need a capability that is not described here, ask Luca directly rather than assuming it is available.

pages.title: Luca, the AI analyst agent
intro: This page describes Luca, the AI analyst agent you use through a chat interface over your connected data. It covers how you ask questions, the kinds of answers you get, and where the agent's limits are. It is for operators and buyers evaluating how Luca would fit day-to-day analysis.
The agent sits on top of Numbers, the reconciled view of your data, and can draw on context you add to the knowledge base. Luca suggests and you decide: it does not change your connected systems.

sections.title: What this page covers
paragraphs: This page covers asking questions in plain English, answers that combine sources, charts generated from a question, follow-up questions, usage without credits, the web app, recommended next steps, marketing content drafts, the done-with-you working model, and how Luca responds to requests outside what it does.
It does not cover connecting sources, which is described under Data connection, or the reconciled dashboard, which is described under Numbers.

sections.title: How you work with Luca
paragraphs: Luca is done-with-you, not done-for-you. Luca does the analysis and proposes a strategy. You validate it and carry it out in your own tools.
During onboarding and data reconciliation, Luca's team works alongside you.

parameters.name: Ask questions in plain English across connected sources
parameters.parameter: Ask questions in plain English across connected sources
parameters.statusDetail: Confirmed from Luca product evidence, founder statements or published policy, as cited below. Not a fresh product test.
parameters.definition: Natural-language questions let you ask about your business in everyday words and get an answer from your data, without writing queries or building reports.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: A chat interface where you type a question in plain English and Luca answers using your connected data.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca is used through a chat interface, Luca Web Chat, over your connected data. New users connect a data source and start chatting with Luca.
Questions can draw on whichever sources your account has connected.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: It helps you get to an answer without waiting for an analyst or switching between tools. A third-party round-up published in September 2026 described Luca as suited to cross-functional analysis across commerce, marketing, finance, inventory and cash flow.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Each question means logging in to separate tools, exporting data and combining it yourself.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Founders, operators and team leads who need answers from their data but do not want to build reports.

parameters.example: Connect two sources, then ask one question that needs both, for example how a recent change in marketing relates to sales. Check whether the answer draws on both sources and whether you can follow it up in the same conversation.
parameters.boundary: Luca can only answer from sources your account has connected. It answers questions; it does not change anything in those sources.
parameters.review: Attach a screenshot of Luca Web Chat showing a sample question and answer.

evidence.fact: Luca is used through a chat interface ('Luca Web Chat') over the user's connected data.
evidence.source: Luca Labs investor presentation, May 2026 — Connect & Setup product screenshot (slide 5)

evidence.fact: Organic users connect a data source and start chatting with Luca.
A September 2026 third-party round-up (Rivo) describes Luca as suited to cross-functional analysis across commerce, marketing, finance, inventory and cash flow.
evidence.source: Rivo / Saras '10 Best AI Analytics Tools for Shopify Brands', 2026-09-26

parameters.name: Answers that combine marketing, finance and commerce data
parameters.parameter: Answers that combine marketing, finance and commerce data
parameters.statusDetail: Confirmed to exist, in the narrower form stated in the scope note. Wider availability is listed for Luca to confirm.
parameters.scope: Answers can only span the sources the account has connected and that Luca's team has reconciled.
parameters.definition: Cross-source reasoning means one answer draws on several kinds of business data at once, such as marketing, finance and commerce, instead of reporting from one tool at a time.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: Answers that bring together data from more than one area of your business in a single response.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca is designed as one main orchestrator with tools beneath it. It reasons across your business's sources rather than one tool at a time.
Answers can only span the sources your account has connected and that Luca's team has reconciled.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: It addresses a common problem: data is fragmented across tools, with no coherent reasoning layer across them. One answer across areas helps you see how a decision in one area relates to another.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Each tool reports on its own slice, and you are left to join the pieces and explain any differences yourself.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Leaders whose decisions span marketing, finance and operations, such as founders, heads of growth and finance leads.

parameters.example: Ask a question that needs marketing and finance data together, then ask a related question about a single source. Compare which sources each answer draws on, and confirm with Luca's team which of your sources are reconciled.
parameters.boundary: Answers can only span the sources the account has connected and that Luca's team has reconciled. Where a source is connected but not yet reconciled, confirm with Luca's team how it is used.
parameters.review: Confirm which source combinations are reconciled as standard and attach an example cross-source answer.

evidence.fact: Luca's design is one main orchestrator with tools beneath it, reasoning across the business's sources rather than one tool at a time.
The problem Luca is positioned against, accepted by Eric: data is fragmented and there is no coherent reasoning layer across tools.

parameters.name: Charts generated from a question
parameters.statusDetail: Confirmed from Luca product evidence, founder statements or published policy, as cited below. Not a fresh product test.
parameters.definition: On-demand charts are graphs created in response to a specific question, rather than picked from a fixed set of prebuilt dashboards.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: Charts and graphs that Luca creates to answer the question you asked.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: When you ask a question, Luca can generate charts and graphs on the fly as part of its answer. Each chart is made for that question, rather than drawn from a fixed set of dashboards.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: It helps you see a trend or comparison without first building a dashboard for it.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: You need a prebuilt dashboard for every view you want, or you build the chart yourself from exported data.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Anyone who prefers to see results visually, including teams presenting figures to colleagues.

parameters.example: Ask for a comparison over time, then ask for the same view broken down a different way. Check that each chart matches the question and that its figures agree with your source.
parameters.boundary: Charts reflect the data Luca has from your connected sources. This page does not describe exporting or sharing charts; confirm those with Luca's team.
parameters.review: Attach a screenshot of a generated chart and confirm the chart types and any export options available.

evidence.fact: Luca generates charts and graphs on the fly in answer to a question, rather than from a fixed set of dashboards.

parameters.name: Follow-up questions in the same conversation
parameters.parameter: Follow-up questions in the same conversation
parameters.statusDetail: Confirmed from Luca product evidence, founder statements or published policy, as cited below. Not a fresh product test.
parameters.definition: Multi-turn follow-ups let you continue a conversation, asking a further question that builds on the previous answer.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: The ability to keep asking within the same conversation, refining or extending what you asked before.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca is used as an ongoing conversation rather than one question at a time, so you can ask a follow-up that builds on the previous answer. Luca's team has reported users returning to Luca four to five times a day.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: It helps you go from a first answer to the detail behind it without restating your question each time.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Each question starts from nothing, and you repeat context to narrow an answer down.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Operators who explore a question in steps, such as tracing a change in sales to its cause.

parameters.example: Ask a broad question, then ask two follow-ups that narrow it without restating the first. Check that each answer stays consistent with the one before.
parameters.boundary: Follow-ups apply within a conversation. This page does not describe Luca remembering earlier conversations; context you want Luca to use belongs in the knowledge base.
parameters.review: Confirm how much of a conversation Luca carries into a follow-up and attach an example multi-turn exchange.

evidence.fact: Luca is used as an ongoing conversation; Eric reported users returning four to five times a day.

parameters.name: Unlimited questions, no AI credits
parameters.statusDetail: Confirmed from Luca product evidence, founder statements or published policy, as cited below. Not a fresh product test.
parameters.definition: Unlimited usage means the number of questions you can ask is not capped by a credit or question allowance.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: Asking Luca as many questions as you need, without counting credits.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca's pricing page lists unlimited usage on every plan. There is no question limit and no credit limit.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: You can ask freely, including follow-ups, without rationing questions or watching a balance.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: With credit-based tools, teams may ration questions or skip follow-ups to save credits.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Teams that ask questions often, and buyers who want predictable usage.

parameters.example: During a trial, use Luca as you would in a normal week, including follow-ups, and check whether any credit counter or question limit appears. Confirm the current terms on the pricing page.
parameters.boundary: This describes usage as listed on the pricing page. Plans differ in other ways, such as seats; check the pricing page for current plan details.
parameters.review: Confirm this wording matches the current pricing page and whether any fair-use terms apply.

evidence.fact: The pricing page lists unlimited usage on every plan, with no question or credit limit.

parameters.name: Web app
parameters.statusDetail: Confirmed from Luca product evidence, founder statements or published policy, as cited below. Not a fresh product test.
parameters.definition: A web app runs in your browser, so there is nothing to install.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: Luca's browser-based application.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca runs as a web application at app.ask-luca.com. You sign in there to use the chat and see your data.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: You can use Luca from a browser without installing software.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Each user would need installed software, which adds setup for a team.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Every Luca user.

parameters.example: Open app.ask-luca.com in the browser your team normally uses and sign in. Check that the chat and your connected data load as expected.
parameters.boundary: This page describes the web app only. Confirm with Luca's team whether any other apps are available.
parameters.review: Confirm supported browsers and attach a screenshot of the signed-in app.

evidence.fact: Luca runs as a web application at app.ask-luca.com.

parameters.name: Recommended next steps
parameters.statusDetail: Confirmed from Luca product evidence, founder statements or published policy, as cited below. Not a fresh product test.
parameters.definition: Prescriptive next steps are recommendations about what to do, given alongside the analysis that supports them.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: Recommendations and step-by-step plans that Luca produces alongside its answers.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca produces recommendations and step-by-step plans, not only numbers. It does the analysis and proposes the strategy.
You validate the plan and carry it out yourself.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: It helps you move from an answer to a decision, with a plan you can review before acting.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: You get figures but must work out on your own what they mean for your next decision.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Founders and operators who want a starting point for action that they can check and adapt.

parameters.example: Ask Luca what you should do about a specific issue in your data. Check whether the plan is broken into steps and whether each step traces back to the analysis. Decide which steps you would carry out.
parameters.boundary: Recommendations are suggestions. Luca does not carry them out; you validate and execute them.
parameters.review: Attach an example recommendation with its step-by-step plan.

evidence.fact: Luca produces recommendations and step-by-step plans, not only numbers.
Luca is done-with-you: it does the analysis and proposes the strategy; the operator validates and executes.

parameters.name: Marketing content drafting
parameters.statusDetail: Confirmed to exist, in the narrower form stated in the scope note. Wider availability is listed for Luca to confirm.
parameters.scope: A secondary capability; output is a draft for the team to review.
parameters.definition: Content drafting produces first versions of marketing material, such as posts or newsletters, for a person to review and edit.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: Drafts of marketing content that Luca can produce on request.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Content generation is listed in Luca's product walkthrough and covers posts, newsletters, images and brand assets. It is a secondary capability, and what Luca produces is a draft for your team to review.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: It can give your team a starting point to edit.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Your team starts each piece from a blank page.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Small marketing teams and founders who write their own content.

parameters.example: Ask Luca for a draft newsletter on a topic from your data. Review it against your brand guidelines and note how much editing it needs.
parameters.boundary: A secondary capability; output is a draft for the team to review. Luca does not publish or send content.
parameters.review: Confirm which content types are available today and attach an example draft.

evidence.fact: Content generation (posts, newsletters, images and brand assets) is listed in Luca's product walkthrough.
evidence.source: Weekly call, 2026-10-02 (Numbers demo and Usman's product walkthrough)

parameters.name: Done-with-you analysis and strategy
parameters.statusDetail: Confirmed from Luca product evidence, founder statements or published policy, as cited below. Not a fresh product test.
parameters.definition: A done-with-you model means the product does the analysis and proposes a strategy, while your team validates it and carries it out.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: The way Luca works with you: Luca analyses and proposes, and you decide and act.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca is done-with-you, not done-for-you. Luca does the analysis and strategy, and you validate and execute.
Luca's team also works alongside clients during onboarding and data reconciliation.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: It keeps decisions with the people accountable for them, while taking analysis work off their plate.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Teams either do all the analysis themselves or hand decisions to a tool they cannot check.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Operators who want analytical help but want to stay in control of what happens in their business.

parameters.example: During onboarding, note which reconciliation tasks Luca's team takes on and which need your input. After setup, take one proposed strategy and check how easily you can validate it before acting.
parameters.boundary: Luca does not execute changes. The work Luca's team does is part of onboarding and reconciliation; confirm its extent for your account.
parameters.review: Confirm what Luca's team does during onboarding and reconciliation, and how that support is scoped.

evidence.fact: Luca is done-with-you, not done-for-you: Luca does the analysis and strategy and the operator validates and executes.
Luca's team works alongside clients during onboarding and data reconciliation.

parameters.name: Tells you plainly when a request is outside what it does
parameters.parameter: Tells you plainly when a request is outside what it does
parameters.statusDetail: Confirmed from Luca product evidence, founder statements or published policy, as cited below. Not a fresh product test.
parameters.definition: Clear refusal means an assistant says directly when a request is outside what it can do, rather than attempting it or giving a vague reply.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: Luca's behaviour when you ask for something it does not do.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: When Luca was asked to automate a change in Shopify or Meta, it replied that it could not. It offered to explain how to make the change, and said a human stays in the loop.
Luca's awareness of its own limits comes from an internal knowledge base written by its team.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: It helps you trust what Luca does say, because it is clear about what it will not do.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: An assistant might appear to attempt a task it cannot complete, leaving you unsure what happened.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Anyone relying on Luca for decisions, and anyone responsible for the systems it connects to.

parameters.example: Ask Luca to make a change in one of your connected systems, such as editing a product. Check that it says it cannot and offers guidance instead.
parameters.boundary: This describes how Luca responds; it does not mean Luca can make changes on request. The exact wording of a response can vary.
parameters.review: Attach a screenshot of a current refusal response to confirm this behaviour.

related.title: Control and safety: Luca reads, you decide

evidence.fact: When asked to automate a change in Shopify or Meta, Luca replied that it could not, offered to explain how to do it, and said a human stays in the loop.

pages.title: Numbers: the reconciled control centre
intro: Numbers is the reconciled control centre in Luca. It brings data from your sources together into one clean database and shows it as a unified view above the chat. This page is for operators and finance or growth leads who want to understand what Numbers shows and how it is set up.
Numbers is the data layer: the dashboard is the reconciled data itself, with no AI in it. Luca, the agent, sits on top of it and answers questions using that data.

sections.title: What this page covers
paragraphs: This page covers the reconciled database, the control-centre view, net revenue, cohort analysis, active and lapsed customers, subscription skip data, reconciliation with accounting data, and the data connections shown on Numbers.
Several of these are delivered through reconciliation work by Luca's team, not created automatically when you connect a source. Each item below says where that applies.

sections.title: How Numbers is set up
paragraphs: Reconciliation is a project led by Luca's team. For the first Numbers client, reconciling Shopify, Recharge and accounting data took about three weeks of work by Luca's team.
Luca's team is rolling Numbers out for several clients. The work needed for your account depends on your sources, so confirm the plan with Luca's team.

parameters.name: One reconciled database across your sources
parameters.parameter: One reconciled database across your sources
parameters.section: 3.2 Data unification, accuracy and trust in the numbers (18)
parameters.statusDetail: Confirmed from Luca product evidence, founder statements or published policy, as cited below. Not a fresh product test.
parameters.definition: A reconciled database combines data from several systems and resolves differences between them, so each figure has one agreed value.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: The single, clean database behind Numbers, built from your sources.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Numbers reconciles your Shopify, subscription and accounting data into one clean database and shows it as a unified view. Luca's team is rolling Numbers out for several clients.
Reconciliation is work led by Luca's team, as described under Reconciled with accounting data.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: It helps you work from one set of figures rather than reconciling differences between tools yourself.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Each system reports its own version of the same figure, and teams spend time explaining the gaps.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Brands whose figures differ between their store, subscription and accounting systems, and the finance and growth leads who reconcile them.

parameters.example: Pick one figure you already track, such as last month's revenue, and compare the value in Numbers with your store and accounting systems. Ask Luca's team to explain any difference.
parameters.boundary: Numbers reconciles the sources included in your reconciliation, which Luca's team sets up. It is not created automatically when you connect a source.
parameters.review: Confirm which source types are included in a standard Numbers setup and attach a screenshot.

Luca, the agent, sits on top of it and answers questions using that data.

answers.question: What happens without it?

answers.question: Who is it for?

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Net revenue is part of the reconciled commerce view in Numbers. Because it comes from reconciled data, it reflects one agreed set of figures rather than a single tool's report.

answers.question: How does it help?

pages.title: Knowledge base and business context
intro: The knowledge base is where you give Luca context about your business. You can upload company documents and manage them in the product. This page is for operators who want Luca's answers to reflect their goals and rules, not only their raw data.
The knowledge base works alongside your connected sources and Numbers. Separately, Luca has its own internal knowledge base, written by its team, that describes what it can and cannot do.

sections.title: What this page covers
paragraphs: This page covers uploading company documents, the kinds of business context the knowledge base holds, and Luca's internal knowledge of its own capabilities.
The knowledge base holds what you upload. It does not describe Luca remembering past conversations, and holding context such as seasonality is not forecasting.

sections.title: What context to add
paragraphs: Luca's website lists goals, constraints, cost rules, lead times and seasonality as the context the knowledge base holds. This context can come from documents such as PDFs or emails that you upload.
Confirm with Luca's team how each type of context is applied in answers.

pages.title: Capital, and how it relates to Luca
intro: This page explains how capital relates to Luca. Capital is optional, and you do not need it to use Luca. It is for buyers and finance leads who want a clear picture before evaluating the product.

Luca is an agentic AI company for e-commerce, not a financing company, and Luca is not a lender or a bank. Capital is an optional output of Luca's intelligence, provided through lending partners, and availability and terms are confirmed directly with Luca's team.

sections.title: What this page covers
paragraphs: This page covers two points: capital is optional, and Luca is not a lender. Any capital is provided through lending partners.
This page does not describe availability, amounts, rates, eligibility, timings or terms, and none of these should be inferred from it.

sections.title: Availability and terms
paragraphs: Whether capital is available to your business, and on what terms, is confirmed directly with Luca's team. Nothing on this page is an offer of credit.
Luca does not lead with capital. The product is built for operators who want to understand and run their business, and every part of it can be used without capital.

parameters.name: Capital is optional
parameters.statusDetail: Confirmed from Luca product evidence, founder statements or published policy, as cited below. Not a fresh product test.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca is an agentic AI company for e-commerce, not a financing company. Capital is a feature that Luca's intelligence can unlock, not a parallel product, and any capital is provided through lending partners.
Whether capital is available to you, and on what terms, is confirmed directly with Luca's team.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: Keeping capital optional means you can use Luca fully for analysis without any funding conversation.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Nothing changes: you do not need capital to use Luca, and choosing not to explore it does not limit the rest of the product.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Every Luca user, since capital is not required. If you want to explore capital, speak to Luca's team directly.

pages.title: Data connection and setup
intro: This page explains how you connect a data source to Luca. It is for anyone setting up an account or evaluating how much effort setup takes.
Connected sources are what the Luca agent reasons across and what Numbers reconciles. Some reconciliation work is done by Luca's team after you connect, as described on the Numbers page.

sections.title: What this page covers
paragraphs: This page covers connecting a standard source through the platform's own sign-in and permission screen, and when you connect your first source.
It does not cover reconciliation, which is separate work described on the Numbers page, or the access permissions Luca holds, which are described under Control and safety.

parameters.name: Connect a source in two clicks (OAuth)
parameters.parameter: Connect a source in two clicks (OAuth)
parameters.statusDetail: Confirmed from Luca product evidence, founder statements or published policy, as cited below. Not a fresh product test.
parameters.definition: OAuth connection lets you link a data source by signing in on that platform's own screen and approving the access it requests.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: A way to connect a data source through the platform's own sign-in and permission screen, rather than by entering that platform's credentials into Luca.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Standard sources connect through each platform's own sign-in and permission screen. Luca's pricing page describes this as two clicks per source for most users.
New users connect a data source during signup, so the first source is in place before they start asking questions.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: It keeps setup short, and you approve access on a platform you already use, which helps you see what you are granting.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Without a direct connection, you would rely on manual exports that go out of date and must be refreshed by hand.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Anyone setting up a Luca account, including founders and operators who do not have a data team.

parameters.example: During signup, connect one standard source and count the steps from choosing it to seeing it listed as connected. Note which permissions the platform's screen asks you to approve. Repeat for a second source to check the experience is consistent.
parameters.boundary: Two clicks applies to standard sources for most users, as described on the pricing page; some sources may need more steps or help from Luca's team. Connecting a source is not the same as reconciling it, which is separate work for Numbers.
parameters.review: Attach a screenshot of the connection flow and confirm which sources use this flow and which need assistance from Luca's team.

evidence.fact: Standard sources connect through each platform's own sign-in and permission screen; the pricing page describes it as two clicks per source for most users.

pages.title: Control and safety: Luca reads, you decide
intro: This page explains what Luca can and cannot do in your connected systems. It is for operators, finance leads and anyone responsible for the systems Luca connects to.
Luca reads, you decide. The agent analyses your data and suggests next steps; you validate them and make any changes yourself.

sections.title: What this page covers
paragraphs: This page covers two principles: nothing changes in a connected system without you, and Luca is read-only by design.
It does not cover how to connect a source, which is described under Data connection.

sections.title: What this means in practice
paragraphs: When Luca was asked to automate a change in Shopify or Meta, it replied that it could not. It offered to explain how to make the change, and said a human stays in the loop.
If you ask Luca to change something, expect guidance on how to do it yourself, not the change itself.

parameters.name: Nothing changes without your approval
parameters.statusDetail: Confirmed from Luca product evidence, founder statements or published policy, as cited below. Not a fresh product test.
parameters.definition: Approval by default means no change is made in a connected system unless a person has decided to make it.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: Luca's principle that you stay in control of every change in your connected systems.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca's website states that every action needs approval by default. In practice, Luca suggests and a human stays in the loop.
Nothing changes in a connected system without you, and you make any changes yourself.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: It helps you act on suggestions on your own terms, so changes happen only when you decide to make them.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: A tool that changes systems on its own could make changes you did not intend.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Operators, finance leads and anyone accountable for live systems.

parameters.example: Ask Luca to make a change in a connected system. Check that it does not make the change and instead suggests what you could do.
parameters.boundary: Luca suggests; it does not make changes in your connected systems on its own. Confirm with Luca's team what the approval-by-default statement covers in the current product.
parameters.review: Confirm what the website's approval-by-default statement refers to in the product today.

evidence.fact: Nothing changes in a connected system without the user: Luca suggests, and a human stays in the loop.
The website states that every action needs approval by default.

parameters.name: Read-only by design
parameters.statusDetail: Confirmed from Luca product evidence, founder statements or published policy, as cited below. Not a fresh product test.
parameters.definition: Read-only access lets a system view data in another system without being able to change it.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: Luca's design principle: it reads your connected data but does not write to it.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca is agent-readable, not agent-writable. It reads your connected data, gets context and reasons over it.
Luca's privacy policy states that its Google access is read-only. Luca's team has said it will not make Luca write to live systems without strong guardrails and audit trails.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: It limits what Luca does in your systems to reading, which helps when you assess the risk of connecting them.

pages.title: Solutions by buyer
intro: This section describes Luca from the point of view of specific buyers: founders and CEOs, subscription brands, finance leads, growth teams, Shopify and Amazon sellers, European and UK brands, and Mastercard Business Bonus merchants. Each page takes the needs that buyer tends to raise and answers them with what Luca does today.
The capabilities themselves are documented under Products and Integrations. Solution pages connect those capabilities to the questions a particular buyer asks during evaluation.

sections.title: Choosing a page
paragraphs: Start with the page that matches your role or business model. Founders and CEOs of Shopify brands will find the overview of how Luca is used day to day. Finance leads will find reconciliation, accounting connections and data retention. Growth teams will find Slack access and Google data sources.

Subscription brands, Shopify and Amazon sellers, European and UK brands, and Mastercard Business Bonus merchants each have their own page covering the needs specific to them. You can read more than one: the pages describe the same product.

sections.title: How to read a solution page
paragraphs: Each need is written as the buyer would put it, then answered: what it is, how it works in Luca, how it helps, what happens without it and who it is for. Each one also gives a test you can run during setup and states its limits.
Where a need is only partly covered today, the page says so and tells you what to confirm with Luca's team.

pages.title: For founders and CEOs of Shopify brands
intro: This page is for founders and CEOs of Shopify brands who want to understand the business without building dashboards or hiring an analyst first. It covers how you use Luca, what it can see, how your data is treated and who helps you get started.
Most of what is described here runs on Numbers, Luca's reconciled view of the business, and on the plain English questions you ask over your connected data.

sections.title: What this page covers
paragraphs: This page covers ten founder needs: one view of the business, plain English answers, the analyst you cannot yet hire, human approval, data use, working on your own data from the first session, data beyond Shopify, connected sources instead of file exports, a conversational way of working, and direct onboarding by Luca's team.
It does not cover pricing figures, which are on Luca's pricing page, or individual integrations, which are documented under Integrations.

sections.title: How founders use Luca
paragraphs: You connect your store and other sources, then ask Luca questions as you would ask an analyst. Luca answers from the connected data and generates charts as it goes. Luca does not change anything in your connected systems; you decide what to do with the answer.

parameters.name: One place to see the whole business
parameters.parameter: One place to see the whole business
parameters.section: 5.1 Founder / CEO of a Shopify DTC brand, ~$1M–$15M — 35 parameters
parameters.statusDetail: Confirmed from Luca product evidence, founder statements or published policy, as cited below. Not a fresh product test.
parameters.definition: A single view that brings a brand's data together so the business can be read in one place. In Luca, this view is called Numbers.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: Numbers, Luca's reconciled view of the business, built from the data you connect.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca reconciles your connected sources into one view, called Numbers. You open Numbers when you want the overall picture, instead of checking each tool in turn, and you can ask Luca questions about what you see.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: It helps you start the day from one set of figures rather than several tools that may not agree.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: You check each system separately and work out yourself why their figures differ.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Founders and CEOs who want to read the whole business quickly, without building reports.

parameters.example: During setup, ask Luca's team which of your sources Numbers will reconcile. Once it is ready, compare one week of revenue in Numbers with the same week in your store and accounting system, and ask Luca to explain any difference.
parameters.boundary: Numbers shows the sources you have connected and that have been reconciled for your account. Luca does not send you this view automatically; you open it or ask for it.
parameters.review: Luca's team should attach a Numbers screenshot and confirm which sources it includes by default.

evidence.fact: Numbers gives one reconciled view of the business.
evidence.source: Weekly call, 2026-10-02 (Numbers demo and Usman's product walkthrough)

parameters.name: Answers in plain English, no dashboards
parameters.parameter: Answers in plain English, no dashboards

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: It helps you get to an answer without learning a reporting tool or waiting for someone to build a view.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: You build and maintain dashboards, or export data and work through it in a spreadsheet.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Founders who want answers, not reporting projects.

parameters.example: Once your store is connected, ask a question you normally answer from a dashboard, such as last month's revenue by channel. Check the chart Luca generates against the figure you already trust.
parameters.boundary: Luca answers from connected data only. If a source is not connected, Luca cannot answer questions that depend on it.
parameters.review: Luca's team should attach an example question with its generated chart.

evidence.fact: Questions are asked in plain English over connected data, with charts generated on the fly.

pages.title: For subscription DTC brands
intro: This page is for subscription DTC brands that need their subscription platform, Shopify and accounting data to agree. It covers reconciled reporting, subscriber status, skip analysis, cohort visibility and connecting a subscription platform.
These needs are met through Numbers, the reconciled view of the business, with the subscription connection set up by Luca's team.

sections.title: What this page covers
paragraphs: This page covers five subscription needs, based on work with live subscription clients that use Recharge. Recharge is the subscription platform confirmed so far, and its connection is set up by Luca's team.
Other subscription platforms, such as Skio and Stay.ai, are not documented in this version. Confirm them with Luca's team before you rely on them.

sections.title: Why reconciliation comes first
paragraphs: Subscriber status, skip history and cohort views only became visible for Luca's subscription clients after their Shopify, Recharge and accounting data was reconciled. Expect reconciliation to be the first piece of work in your setup.

parameters.name: Subscriptions, Shopify and accounting reconciled
parameters.statusDetail: Confirmed from Luca product evidence, founder statements or published policy, as cited below. Not a fresh product test.
parameters.definition: Bringing subscription platform, store and accounting data into agreement so that one view of the business can be trusted.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: A single reconciled view of subscription, Shopify and accounting data.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: For a subscription client, Luca reconciled Shopify, Recharge and accounting data into one view in Numbers. You then ask questions over the reconciled figures.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: It helps you work from one set of subscription figures rather than three systems that may disagree.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Your subscription platform, store and accounts each tell a different story, and you reconcile them by hand.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Subscription DTC brands running Shopify with a subscription platform and an accounting system.

parameters.example: During setup, choose one recent month and ask Luca's team to show how the reconciled view matches your subscription platform and your accounts for that month.
parameters.boundary: Confirmed for Shopify, Recharge and accounting data. The subscription connection is set up by Luca's team, and other subscription platforms are to confirm.
parameters.review: Luca's team should attach a screenshot of the reconciled subscription view and confirm which accounting systems were involved.

evidence.fact: For a subscription client, Shopify, Recharge and accounting data were reconciled into one view.
evidence.source: Weekly call, 2026-10-02 (Numbers demo and Usman's product walkthrough)

parameters.name: Active and lapsed subscribers
parameters.statusDetail: Confirmed from Luca product evidence, founder statements or published policy, as cited below. Not a fresh product test.
parameters.definition: Knowing how many subscribers are currently active and how many have become inactive.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: A view of active versus inactive subscribers.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Once subscription, Shopify and accounting data were reconciled, active versus inactive subscribers became visible in Numbers. You can then ask Luca about either group.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: It helps you see the real size of your active subscriber base and how many have lapsed.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: You rely on platform counts that may not match orders or revenue.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Subscription brands tracking the health of their subscriber base.

parameters.example: After reconciliation, ask Luca how many subscribers are active and how many are inactive. Compare the result with your subscription platform's own count and ask Luca to explain any gap.
parameters.boundary: This view depends on reconciliation being complete for your account. How active and inactive are defined should be confirmed with Luca's team.
parameters.review: Luca's team should confirm the definitions of active and inactive used in Numbers.

evidence.fact: Active versus inactive subscribers became visible after reconciliation.
evidence.source: Weekly call, 2026-10-02 (Numbers demo and Usman's product walkthrough)

parameters.name: Skips analysed (the $72,000 case)
parameters.statusDetail: Confirmed from Luca product evidence, founder statements or published policy, as cited below. Not a fresh product test.
parameters.definition: Analysing when subscribers skip deliveries, and what those skips mean for revenue.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: Analysis of subscription skip history and its effect on revenue.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca rebuilds subscription skip history from your data. For one client, the rebuilt history revealed a $72,000 revenue shortfall.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: It helps you see revenue that skips quietly remove, which can be hard to spot in platform reports.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Skips can reduce revenue without showing up clearly in your reporting.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Subscription brands that allow customers to skip deliveries.

parameters.example: Ask Luca's team to rebuild skip history for a recent quarter, then ask Luca how much revenue skips affected in that period and how that compares with your expectations.
parameters.boundary: The $72,000 figure is one client's result, not an expected outcome. This page documents skips; pause analysis is not documented in this version.
parameters.review: Luca's team should confirm whether pauses are analysed alongside skips and how skip history is rebuilt.

evidence.fact: Rebuilt subscription-skip history revealed a $72,000 revenue shortfall for one client.

parameters.name: Cohort retention
parameters.statusDetail: Confirmed from Luca product evidence, founder statements or published policy, as cited below. Not a fresh product test.
parameters.definition: Grouping subscribers into cohorts and following how each cohort is retained over time.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: Cohort visibility for subscription brands.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: It helps you see whether newer subscribers are retained better or worse than earlier ones.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: You see total subscribers but not how each group behaves over time.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Subscription brands judging retention and acquisition quality.

parameters.example: After reconciliation, ask Luca to show retention for two cohorts that started at different times, and check whether the difference matches what you see in the business.
parameters.boundary: This page confirms cohort visibility in Numbers. Exact cohort definitions, such as grouping by start month, should be confirmed with Luca's team.
parameters.review: Luca's team should confirm how cohorts are defined and attach a cohort view screenshot.

evidence.fact: Cohort visibility was the stated gap Numbers closed.
evidence.source: Weekly call, 2026-10-02 (Numbers demo and Usman's product walkthrough)

pages.title: For CFOs and finance leads
intro: This page is for CFOs, finance leads and fractional CFOs evaluating whether Luca's numbers can be trusted and controlled. It covers approval and control, the role of your accounting system, data retention, reconciliation to the accounting system and accounting connections.

answers.question: What happens without it?

pages.title: Pricing model
intro: This page explains how Luca's pricing is structured: what you pay for, what does not change your price and how billing works. It is for founders and finance leads comparing Luca with other analytics tools or with hiring an analyst.

sections.title: What this page covers
paragraphs: This page covers the pricing model: seat-based pricing, usage, integration fees, annual billing and how to think about cost against hiring. It does not list plan names, prices, discount sizes or trial terms, because those change.

sections.title: The model at a glance
paragraphs: Luca prices by seat. Store revenue, order volume and ad spend do not set the price, so the plan price does not rise as your brand grows.

pages.title: How Luca stores and processes your data
intro: This page explains where Luca hosts your data, how each customer's data is kept separate, which sub-processors handle it and whether it is used to train AI models. It is for anyone assessing Luca as a vendor.
It summarises Luca's privacy policy and website. For access scopes and deletion, see Access and deletion.

sections.title: What this page covers
paragraphs: This page covers hosting, the separation of customer data, credential storage, named sub-processors and model training. It reflects ask-luca.com/privacy and ask-luca.com as read on 16 October 2026.
It does not cover certifications. Ask Luca's team for security documentation, or about anything your review needs that is not listed here.

sections.title: Summary
paragraphs: Infrastructure runs on Google Cloud Platform. Each customer's data sits in a separate BigQuery dataset, and credentials are kept in Google Secret Manager.

The privacy policy names OpenAI and Google Cloud Platform as sub-processors. OpenAI processes data under enterprise terms that exclude training on it, and the website states that Luca does not train third-party foundation models on customers' financials.

parameters.name: Customer data kept separate
parameters.statusDetail: Confirmed from Luca product evidence, founder statements or published policy, as cited below. Not a fresh product test.
parameters.definition: Tenant isolation is the practice of storing each customer's data apart from other customers' data in a shared service.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: It is how a service used by many customers keeps one customer's data apart from another's. It is a standard question in a vendor review.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Each customer's data sits in its own BigQuery dataset on Google Cloud Platform.
Credentials you provide when you connect platforms are kept in Google Secret Manager. Both points are stated in Luca's privacy policy at ask-luca.com/privacy.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: This helps you answer the data separation question in a vendor review with a specific storage model rather than a general assurance.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Without a stated separation model, you would need to ask how your data is stored relative to other customers before you could complete a review.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Founders, finance leads and anyone completing a security or vendor questionnaire for their brand.

parameters.example: During setup or a trial, ask your reviewer to read the dataset and credential statements in the privacy policy. Then send Luca's team any follow-up questions your questionnaire requires and record their answers alongside the policy wording.
parameters.boundary: This describes how data is stored. It is not a certification or audit result. Request security documentation from Luca's team if your review needs it.
parameters.review: Confirm the wording matches the current privacy policy, and decide whether to attach an architecture diagram or security documentation.

evidence.fact: Each customer's data sits in a separate BigQuery dataset on Google Cloud Platform; credentials are kept in Google Secret Manager.

Retention periods for data other than Google data are set out in the privacy policy at ask-luca.com/privacy, not on this page.

sections.title: Checking access when you connect
paragraphs: When you connect a platform, read the permission screen that platform shows before you approve. For connectors other than Google, that screen is where you see what Luca is requesting.

parameters.name: Deletion and retention after you disconnect
parameters.parameter: Deletion and retention after you disconnect
parameters.statusDetail: Confirmed from Luca product evidence, founder statements or published policy, as cited below. Not a fresh product test.
parameters.definition: Retention and deletion rules set out how long a vendor keeps your data and when it is removed after you stop using the service.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: It is the vendor's stated timing for removing your data after you disconnect a platform or close your account.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Data from Google connections is deleted within 30 days of disconnecting.
For other data, Luca's privacy policy states how long it is retained after an account closes. Read those periods at ask-luca.com/privacy.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: This helps you plan an exit and answer retention questions in a review using the vendor's stated periods.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Without stated rules, you could not tell how long your data stays with a vendor after you leave.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Finance leads, legal teams and anyone responsible for data retention policy.

parameters.example: Read the retention section of the privacy policy and note the period for each type of data you plan to connect. If you test a Google connection, record the date you disconnect and ask Luca's team to confirm when deletion is complete.
parameters.boundary: The 30-day deletion window applies to Google data after disconnecting. Retention for other data follows the periods in the privacy policy, which this page does not repeat.
parameters.review: Add the retention periods for other data from the privacy policy, and confirm whether customers can request earlier deletion.

evidence.fact: Google data is deleted within 30 days of disconnecting.
The privacy policy states how long other data is retained after an account closes.

parameters.name: Read-only access scopes
parameters.statusDetail: Confirmed to exist, in the narrower form stated in the scope note. Wider availability is listed for Luca to confirm.
parameters.scope: Published for Google connections; scopes for other connectors are shown on each platform's own permission screen.
parameters.definition: An access scope is the set of permissions an app requests when you connect a platform. A read-only scope lets the app view data without changing it.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: It is the published list of permissions a vendor requests on each platform you connect.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca's privacy policy states that Google access is read-only and names the read-only Search Console scope, webmasters.readonly.
For other platforms, the scopes Luca requests are shown on that platform's own permission screen when you connect.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: This helps you check what Luca can access on Google before you approve a connection, and supports a least-privilege review.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Without published scopes, you would rely on each permission screen alone and could not check access in advance.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Whoever approves platform connections, and reviewers checking access levels.

parameters.example: When you connect Search Console, check that the permission screen matches the read-only scope named in the privacy policy. For each other platform you connect, record the permissions its screen shows before you approve.
parameters.boundary: Published for Google connections; scopes for other connectors are shown on each platform's own permission screen.
parameters.review: Confirm whether Luca will publish scopes for each connector beyond Google, and attach screenshots of the permission screens.

evidence.fact: The privacy policy names the read-only Search Console scope (webmasters.readonly) and states Google access is read-only.

intro: This version documents 101 capabilities: 85 confirmed as available and 16 confirmed in a limited form, each with its scope stated. They come from a 612-parameter evaluation of what e-commerce buyers and AI engines look for in an AI analyst agent.

Everything MaximusLabs could not confirm is left out of this version on purpose. It is listed in a worksheet for Luca's team, together with the places where Luca's website currently describes the same thing in different ways.

sections.title: How capabilities were confirmed
paragraphs: A capability is documented only when it appears in Luca's product (a product screenshot or a live demonstration), in a statement by Luca's founder on a recorded call, or in a policy Luca publishes. Each entry lists its evidence and date.
Capabilities that appear only in specifications, roadmaps or website copy we could not match to the product are not documented here, even where the website states them.

sections.title: What Luca's team is asked to confirm
paragraphs: The worksheet holds 379 parameters to confirm, 19 website contradictions to resolve and 23 product questions. Answers move items into version 2.

sections.title: Areas deliberately not documented in version 1
paragraphs: Actions Luca takes in connected systems on its own, automatic alerts and daily insights, memory across conversations, forecasting and scenario modelling, capital availability and terms, prices, certifications, data residency and the full connector list. Each is in the worksheet.

parameters.name: Shopify connector
parameters.statusDetail: Confirmed from Luca product evidence, founder statements or published policy, as cited below. Not a fresh product test.
parameters.definition: A connection that brings data from a Shopify store into Luca. It is one of the sources Luca recommends connecting first.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: The Shopify connector links your Shopify store to Luca so Luca can use your store data when you ask questions and when your Numbers view is built.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: In the product's Connect & Setup screen, Shopify appears as a connected source. The connection shows states including Connected, Completed and Syncing.
For a live client, Shopify data was reconciled with subscription and accounting data into Numbers.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: It gives Luca your store data as a base. This helps you look at store activity next to the advertising, analytics and finance sources you add later.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: If you sell on Shopify and do not connect it, Luca has no store data to reason across, and Numbers cannot include it.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Brands that run their store on Shopify, and the founders, operators and finance leads who need store data alongside other sources.

parameters.example: During setup, connect Shopify and watch its state in the Connect & Setup screen until it shows as connected. Then ask Luca a question you already know the answer to from your Shopify admin and compare the two.
parameters.boundary: This connector covers Shopify store data only. This page does not list the Shopify data fields read or the store permissions requested; confirm these with Luca.
parameters.review: Attach a current screenshot of the Shopify card in Connect & Setup and confirm the meaning of each connection state. Confirm the data fields and permissions the connection uses.

evidence.fact: Shopify appears as a connected source in Luca's Connect & Setup screen, with connection states Connected, Completed and Syncing.
evidence.source: Luca Labs investor presentation, May 2026 — Connect & Setup product screenshot (slide 5)
